To help understand the concept of inflation theory in cosmology, imagine you have a tiny, wrinkled piece of paper with dots drawn on it to represent galaxies. In the standard Big Bang model, the universe expands like a slowly rising loaf of bread. However, inflation theory suggests that right after the beginning, the universe underwent a phase of exponential growth, similar to taking that tiny, wrinkled paper and instantly stretching it out until it is larger than a football field. During this incredibly brief moment, the space between the dots (galaxies) grew so fast that they moved away from each other faster than light could travel, yet the paper itself didn't break. This rapid stretching smoothed out the wrinkles, explaining why the universe looks so uniform and flat today.
